Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week — OmniHealth's security and procurement teams have a short list of follow-ups focused on how Redwood measures and exposes SLO data. I've attached our standard questionnaire (PDF) with specific asks, but high level we're looking for:

- Exact SLO definitions you use for availability and request latency (percentiles, windows, and whether synthetic checks count)
- How measurements are computed (ingest pipeline, sampling, retention windows)
- Monitoring stack and alerting thresholds we can rely on for our own incident processes
- Whether we can get read-only access to live dashboards and historical telemetry (and what scope you'll allow)
- Any existing exception paths (e.g., scheduled maintenance, planned batch workloads) and how those are handled in SLA calculations

Could you point to the artifacts you can share (dashboards, raw metric exports, alert recipes, data retention policy)? Procurement is also asking for a short note on whether Redwood can grant a temporary view-only Grafana/Looker-style invite for our SREs while the contract is reviewed.

Attachment: Omni_SLO_Questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf, 48KB)

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a 20 minute call if helpful.

Best,
David Liu
Director, Infrastructure 
OmniHealth

David — thanks for sending this along and for the clear list of asks. Looping in Marissa (Customer Success lead) and Karthik (SRE/product) so we can provide the artifacts and the technical detail.

Quick notes up front:
- Our availability SLOs are computed from successful completion of inference requests at p99 latency per 5m rolling window; synthetic probe data is tracked separately and used for regional health checks but excluded from contractual uptime calculations unless noted.
- We retain raw telemetry (request-level traces + metrics) for 90 days and aggregated 1h/24h rollups for 12 months; exports available on request.

Marissa/Karthik — can you attach the SLO proof playbook (short doc), sample Grafana read-only invite instructions, and a representative alerting ruleset? Also please call out how we treat scheduled maintenance and batch-job-caused tail-latency when computing SLA credits.

Irene Choi
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Hi David — attaching the requested artifacts and answering the bullets inline. Forwarding your original questionnaire below.

Attachments: redwood_proof_playbook_v1.docx (55KB); dashboard-readonly-invite.txt (small tokenized invite)

Short answers:
- Definitions: Availability = percentage of successful inference responses within p99 latency threshold measured over 30-day rolling window. Latency SLOs we discuss contractually are p50/p90/p99 by endpoint; default commercial commitment is p99 < 200ms for our text-generation hosted tier (region-dependent). We include details in the playbook (section 2).
- How computed: We compute per-request success and latency at the edge, ingest into time-series (Prometheus->Cortex) and write raw traces to our distributed tracing store. Aggregation performs rolling-window percentiles with reservoir summaries; contractual calculations exclude synthetic probes and internal scheduled maintenance windows.
- Monitoring stack & alerting: Grafana + Cortex for metrics, Tempo for traces, Alertmanager for alert rules. We've included our example alert recipes (error-rate > 0.5% sustained over 5m; p99 latency > threshold for 3 consecutive 1m buckets) in the playbook.
- Read access: We can create time-limited, read-only dashboard invites for customer SREs (Grafana RBAC). Typical scope: per-customer tenant filters, per-region views, and a subset of raw logs. For OmniHealth we can grant a 30-day read-only invite while procurement/contracting completes.
- Exception handling: Planned maintenance is excluded from SLA calculations when scheduled >48 hours in advance and announced. For customer workloads that cause predictable nightly tail-latency (e.g., large batched ingestion), we surface a proposed exception window — usually a negotiated rolling 2-hour window nightly; these are documented and excluded from availability computations if mutually agreed and scheduled.

Links and a temporary invite:
- Playbook: https://redwood.app/drive/teams/omn-health/slo-evidence (drive doc with playbook)
- Temporary invite token (attached): dashboard-readonly-invite.txt — instructions for one-click read access.

If you want a short walkthrough, happy to do a 20m call with your SREs next week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Irene — this is really helpful, thanks. A couple quick follow-ups from procurement and SRE: 

1) We'll take the 30-day read-only invite — please provision for two SRE users (david.liu@omnihealth.com, sophie.tran@omnihealth.com). Please include per-tenant filters so we only see OmniHealth telemetry.

2) Regarding exception windows: OmniHealth runs a heavy batch job nightly between 02:00–03:30 local that historically impacts p99 tail latency. Procurement is open to a negotiated nightly exception but asks two conditions: (a) the exception window must be explicitly listed in the contract with local timezone, and (b) Redwood provides a compensating rollback plan (automatic reroute to a lower-cost tier or traffic shaping) if tail latency causes downstream SLA violations for our end-users. Can you confirm Redwood's recommended exception language and the compensating controls you would offer?

3) Procurement also requested an export of raw 5m rollup CSVs for the last 90 days once we have a signed NDA. Is that a standard path?

If you can drop a short paragraph for each of the three items above (read access provisioning steps, exception contract wording + compensating controls, and CSV export process) we'll fold that into our vendor questionnaire and move to legal. Prefer to keep this via email for traceability; happy to call if anything is unclear.

Best,
David
Director, Infrastructure
OmniHealth
